narrative: Constructed 2026-08-29 as the worked example of the HEARTH language (the wider shelf). A neighbourhood church of about a hundred that runs a food pantry and a Tuesday grief group; the pastor opens with a story about the first Sunday, speaks warmly and slowly, has a green-and-gold logo the deacons love, and wants a nervous first-time visitor to feel held before they feel impressed. Fills library holes: warm_welcomed, vulnerable + curious audience, established_attached maturity, a soft_dark ground, and the portrait_presence hero. Resulting direction: PEOPLE FIRST, LIGHT SECOND — a deep green ground with a warm light that seems to come from inside the page, soft-cornered frames, a humanist serif at moderate scale, real faces in the light, stats as sentences. Teaches: the inner-light radial, soft corners as tone, portrait-led hero, deriving palette from an attached asset, and gentle motion that eases rather than snaps.

evidence: the first Sunday there were eleven of us and a space heater
most of them haven't been in a church in twenty years
they come after a loss or a move; they're checking whether it's safe
I'm not up front; I'm at the door
they want visitors to feel: expected, safe, warm
service times, a people photo, a give button — the trust cues are kept
the green and gold stays; the deacons designed it
Sundays, Tuesdays, the pantry every other Saturday

palette.because: P16: the attached green becomes the deep ground itself, the gold becomes the one warm light; P14: no red, no urgency, soft edges for a vulnerable visitor.

typography.pairing_logic: A humanist serif at moderate scale with a rounded warm sans for body — kinship in warmth (P5, alongside), contrast only in size; one hand-set line in the gold italic for the blessing.
typography.because: A pastor at the door doesn't shout; the type is moderate, warm and close.

layout.because: P6: alongside → two presences — the faces one side, the welcome the other; P7: a novice audience gets one thing per screen and a gentle descent (times, then people, then how to help).

motion.signature_move: the inner light — the warm radial behind the hero slowly brightens and settles, like a room warming up
motion.because: P8/P12: one slow move that restates 'held'; nothing snaps or slides.

hero_concept.concept_statement: Real faces from a real Sunday in a soft-cornered frame, lit from inside the page by a warm radial in the gold; beside them, 'There's a seat for you Sunday at 10' in the humanist serif and one gold italic line — the blessing. A soft pill to plan a visit.
hero_concept.because: story_first + warm_welcomed → people before building, the welcome before the program (P1: meet the vulnerable visitor with warmth).

whitespace.because: Air that feels like a living room, not a lobby — generous line-height, frames close to the words.

notes: the first-Sunday story runs as the about section in full, first person, with the space-heater photo
stats are sentences — 'about a hundred of us, 40 families fed a month' — never monuments
service times sit in a warm card under the hero with the address and a 'what to expect' line
the give button is the same soft pill as plan-a-visit, never louder
voice_to_visual.because: A voice that names people becomes a page that shows them; numbers become sentences because the pastor speaks in them.

rule_break.what: the ground is dark for a church — the convention is white and airy; here the dark green is warm, not grave
rule_break.because: The deacons' green, honoured as the room itself (P16), is the one break inside an otherwise honoured vertical (P9).

tension.pole_b: a place that is actually doing things
tension.expression: The room owns the inner light, the soft corners, the blessing; the doing owns the pantry numbers-as-sentences, the Tuesday group card and the calendar module below the fold.
tension.because: All warmth reads as vague; all activity reads as a bulletin — a good church is both.

first_impression.remember: Real faces in a warm light, and the line about a seat on Sunday.
first_impression.because: warm_welcomed for the vulnerable = expected before impressed.

language.because: A people trade with a warm slow voice, an attached green-and-gold, a vulnerable novice audience and no wish for edge — people first, light second; Arena would shout at someone checking whether it's safe.

distinctiveness_check.notes: Nearest are e4 (warm, humanist, airy, breathing — but a pale organic page with an environment hero) and e1 (single warm accent, asymmetric, airy — but deep-dark editorial serif with a metaphor hero); this is the only soft-dark ground and the only portrait-presence hero in the library.

summary_for_practitioner: Your site feels like walking into a warm room. The deacons' green becomes the whole ground, and their gold becomes a soft light that seems to come from inside the page, behind real faces from a real Sunday in a rounded frame. Beside them: 'There's a seat for you Sunday at 10,' one gold line of blessing, and a soft button to plan a visit. Your first-Sunday story runs in full in your own words with the space-heater photo; your numbers are sentences — about a hundred of us, forty families fed a month — never big figures. The light warms slowly when the page opens; nothing else moves.
